summary.prose: Story s6 gives each Epic and Story one typed tracker binding on its artifact's envelope, and lets a plan, design, diagram or build, review or test record be attached to the unit's issue as a commit-pinned GitHub link. The tracker port gains listComments and attach (GitHub only, through the gh CLI). Posts to an issue carry a stable marker and are reconciled through listComments before any retry, so a post that succeeded and lost its record is never repeated; a link under the parent that failed stays pending and is retried the next time the unit is ensured.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

ownedContracts.name: TrackerBinding
ownedContracts.purpose: The typed binding between a lifecycle artifact and its tracker issue, the attachments of supporting artifacts, and the tracker port operations to read comments and attach, implemented for the GitHub adapter.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactIdScheme
consumedContracts.purpose: The single place artifact ids are made and recognised: the existing hierarchical typed ids extended for Epic, Story, Task, the Tasks file and diagrams, one story and task form, the folder-name date source, and the functional-requirement id helpers that live in id.ts today.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactEnvelope
consumedContracts.purpose: The common shape of every stored entity and the one reader and writer for it, with References and namespaced Actors.

consumedContracts.name: HistoryRecords
consumedContracts.purpose: The change log entry and the Feedback entry shapes, the persisted sidecar record that carries the owning artifact id, and the append and read API, including how an update says which feedback it addressed.

consumedContracts.name: Lifecycle
consumedContracts.purpose: The typed lifecycle structures, the ten statuses and their transitions, the revision and content-hash rule, the completion roll-up and the conflict check against the log tail.

boundary.internal: The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — feedback and tracker binding

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

api.name: TrackerPort.listComments

parameters.name: since
parameters.purpose: ISO time; only comments created or updated at or after it.

returns.meaning: Every comment of the issue in ascending time order, complete across pages, as { externalId, author, text, at, url? }.

errors.type: PortResult failure (kind unreachable | missing-signin | missing-tool | rejected)
errors.condition: gh cannot be run, is not signed in, or the issue cannot be read; a failed read is a failure, never an empty list.

postconditions: read-only: no comment or issue is changed
implemented for the GitHub adapter only, through gh api; no direct REST call

api.name: TrackerPort.attach
api.signature: attach(issue: IssueRef, artifact: Reference, link: string): PortResult<{ externalId?: string }>

parameters.name: artifact
parameters.purpose: The artifact being attached (entityId, type); names it in the comment text.

parameters.name: link
parameters.purpose: The commit-pinned permalink to the file.

returns.meaning: externalId is the id of the comment that carries the link.

errors.condition: the comment cannot be posted; nothing is known to have been posted when the failure is before the call, and an unconfirmed failure is reconciled by link before a retry.

preconditions: link contains the artifact's file path at a commit
postconditions: GitHub has no attachment API: the adapter posts one comment holding the link; a second attach of the same link is the caller's to avoid by reconciling first

api.name: readBinding
api.signature: readBinding(repoPath: string, artifactId: string): TrackerBinding | undefined

parameters.name: artifactId
parameters.purpose: A lifecycle artifact id (the Define for an Epic, the LLD for a Story until s9 creates Epic and Story artifacts).

returns.meaning: The envelope's binding, or undefined when the artifact has none or does not exist.

errors.condition: meta.envelope.binding is present and malformed; ensureUnitIssueDetailed calls readBinding before its local resolve and returns a before-create failure; resolveUnitIssueLocal, which the gate and the draft hook call, reports no local issue and the gate's ensure then reports the same failure.

postconditions: synchronous and read-only: the team gate reads it on its synchronous path

its callers are the team gate's teamContext, the draft-issue hook's fast path and its 'could not be recorded' result (src/workflow/draft-issues.ts:113-133) and, through teamContext with createIssue false, the handoff check (src/workflow/team/handoff.ts:395)

resolveUnitIssueLocal reads the binding for an Epic or Story unit; with no binding it reads the older epicRef, storyRef or the Define's storyRefs and binds the unit from that ref (a one-way rebind, so no second issue is created for an issue that predates unit labels and artifact-id titles); a Task unit still reads its Plan record. s9 removes the fallback with the old fields

api.name: bindArtifact
api.signature: bindArtifact(repoPath: string, artifactId: string, issue: IssueRef, now?: () => string): BindResult

parameters.name: issue
parameters.purpose: The one issue of the unit.

returns.meaning: { ok: true, binding, created } when the artifact is now bound to this issue (created false when it already was), or { ok: false, reason } when it is bound to a different issue.

errors.condition: the artifact already holds a binding to another issue (a unit has exactly one issue), or the head cannot be read or written.

postconditions: writes meta.envelope.binding { reference: { entityId: issue, type: 'github:issue', relation: 'tracked-by' }, createdAtRevision: the head's revision number, posted: [] } as one meta-only write; the revision number and content hash do not move
a repository with no tracker never reaches this call, so it has no binding

api.name: recordPosted
api.signature: recordPosted(repoPath: string, artifactId: string, kind: PostedKind, externalId?: string, now?: () => string): boolean

parameters.name: externalId
parameters.purpose: The comment id when known (from a reconciled comment).

returns.meaning: True when the kind is now recorded; false when the binding or head could not be written (logged).

postconditions: a kind already recorded is not recorded twice
meta-only; revision unchanged

api.name: setPendingLink
api.signature: setPendingLink(repoPath: string, artifactId: string, link: TrackerBinding['pendingLink']): boolean

parameters.name: link
parameters.type: { parent: Reference; child?: Reference; childId?: number } | undefined
parameters.purpose: The link under the parent that failed, or undefined to clear it once done.

postconditions: a pending link carries at least a child ref or a child id
meta-only; revision unchanged

api.name: attachDocuments
api.signature: attachDocuments(unit: UnitRef, port: TrackerPort, targets: readonly AttachTarget[], deps?: AttachDeps): AttachOutcome

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The unit whose issue receives the links.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The files to attach: a plan, a design document, a diagram or a build, review or test record, each with its repo-relative path.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Seams for git and the clock.

returns.meaning: { attached, reconciled, skipped, failed[] }: links posted now, links found already posted (recorded without a second post), links already recorded, and each failure with its reason.

errors.condition: the file has uncommitted changes, is not tracked, the unit has no binding, or the tracker call fails; none of these throws.

preconditions: the unit's artifact is bound to its issue
the files are committed; git decides, whatever the commitArtifacts setting says
postconditions: the link is blob/<last commit that touched the file>/<path> on the repository's GitHub host
a link already recorded for (target, revision) is skipped; a new revision commits to a new sha, so it adds a new link and the old comment stays
before posting, listComments is searched for the link; a comment holding it is recorded and not posted again
an Attachment { target, revision, at, externalId } is recorded per link as one meta-only write

the Attachment records it writes change the artifact head, so the caller commits them with a second commit; a target that was refused as uncommitted is not recorded and is attached by the next call, which recomputes the targets and skips the recorded ones

api.name: runUnitExtras
api.signature: runUnitExtras(unit: UnitRef, steps: readonly ExtraStep[], deps?: ExtrasDeps): ExtrasOutcome

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The unit the posts belong to.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.purpose: The approve-time posts; a comment step now names the marker its body carries.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Clock, mark writer and a comment lister for reconciliation.

errors.condition: a post fails, or the comment list for reconciliation cannot be read (the post is then not made).

postconditions: a kind already in binding.posted is skipped
for a comment step whose kind is not recorded, listComments is read once and a comment carrying the step's marker is recorded as done and not posted again
a post that succeeded but whose record failed is reported, and the next run reconciles it instead of repeating it
for an Epic or Story the record is the binding's posted list; a Task unit keeps its legacy record until s7

api.name: ensureUnitIssueDetailed
api.signature: ensureUnitIssueDetailed(unit: UnitRef, port: TrackerPort, deps?: EnsureIssueDeps): EnsureResult<EnsuredIssue>

errors.condition: as today: before-create failures create nothing; a failed create is unconfirmed and found again by label or title.
the artifact head that holds the unit's binding cannot be read or written, so the issue could not be recorded; nothing is created.

postconditions: an Epic or Story issue found or created is recorded with bindArtifact on the unit's artifact; a Task issue keeps its record on the Plan until s7
a failed link under the parent is stored with setPendingLink and retried at the next call until it succeeds, then cleared
an issue a person created first is adopted through the label or title lookup and bound the same way

an issue this call creates is bound only after the duplicate check: the unit label is listed first and the lowest-numbered issue is bound once (tieBreak), this call's own issue being commented on and closed as a duplicate when it is not the lowest; when the listing fails the created issue is bound and kept, as today
bindArtifact is therefore called once per unit by a create and never needs to replace a binding; a crash between the create and the bind is found again by the unit label at the next call
when the unit's artifact head cannot be read (malformed binding or missing file) the call returns a before-create failure naming the head, before any issue is looked up or created

api.name: tracker.attach (daemon IPC method)
api.signature: tracker.attach(params: { repo?: string; epicHash: string; storyId?: string }): Promise<AttachOutcome | { error: string }>

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: The repository; falls back to the daemon's INSRC_REPO.

parameters.name: storyId
parameters.purpose: The Story; absent for the Epic's own documents.

returns.meaning: What attachDocuments returned for the unit's design documents, plan and records, or an error for a bad request.

errors.condition: the repository has no tracker or no binding for the unit, or the request is malformed; never a throw

postconditions: resolves the unit's targets (the HLD or LLD and its diagram companions, the plan, and the Story's BUILD, CR and TESTS records) from the artifacts on disk, calls attachDocuments, and commits nothing
a target that is dirty or untracked is reported refused with 'commit the file first'; recorded attachments are skipped, so a later call attaches only what is new

The reference is { entityId: 'owner/repo#N', type: 'github:issue', relation: 'tracked-by' } (an external target with the namespaced external type docs/plans/core-data-model.md names, github:issue, so the store's artifact-id check does not apply). posted holds one entry per kind at most (milestone, task-list, design, review, plan), with the comment id as externalId when it was reconciled or known. Written only by bindArtifact, recordPosted and setPendingLink.

The declared sc6 shape is kept. One entry per (target, revision); target is a Reference { entityId: artifact id, type: its kind, relation: 'documents' }; revision is the artifact's lifecycle revision number when attached; externalId is the comment id. Written only by attachDocuments.
{ externalId: string; author: string; text: string; at: string; url?: string }, the element of listComments' result (the shape the sc6 sketch gives).

dataModelChanges.details: prepareArtifactWrite carries meta.envelope.binding and meta.envelope.attachments from the head already on disk into every content write of an existing artifact, as it carries meta.tracker today; a first write (no head on disk) keeps what the caller gave. So a content write by the store can never undo a binding patched by BindingService, and BindingService is the one writer of both fields after creation.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Implements TrackerBinding and Attachment as declared, and the port additions listComments and attach for the GitHub adapter. Adds the TrackerComment type the sketch implies and the read, bind, record and attach functions that are the only writers of the two envelope fields.

Uses the envelope's binding and attachments fields and their decoding and validation unchanged. The store's write path gains one carry rule for those two fields (carryBinding), which keeps the store a faithful reader and writer of everything else.

Reads the lifecycle revision number for createdAtRevision and for Attachment.revision. A binding or attachment change is a meta-only write, so the revision number and content hash do not move (k3) and the integrity check against the log tail is unaffected.

Maps a unit to its artifact id with ArtifactIds.make (the Define for an Epic, the LLD for a Story, until s9 creates Epic and Story artifacts) and builds the post marker from the artifact id; adds no second title lookup and uses findIssuesByTitleToken as AMD-2f27754d4ad00b8e-6 states.

Does not append to the change log or feedback. Binding and attachment bookkeeping is recorded in the binding itself (posted[].at, attachments[].at) and in the log output; this is a stated deviation from 'every state change appends a change log entry' and is raised as an open question.

errorCases.scenario: The tracker does not answer listComments before a comment step that might already be posted
errorCases.detection: TrackerPort.listComments returns a failed PortResult inside runUnitExtras for the first unrecorded comment step
errorCases.response: The step is reported failed with the tracker's reason and is not posted; the next run tries the read again. An uncertain post is never retried blind.
errorCases.userImpact: The design, review or plan comment is delayed until the tracker answers; no duplicate appears.

errorCases.scenario: A post succeeds and recording it in the binding fails (disk full, head unreadable)
errorCases.detection: recordPosted returns false after the port call succeeded
errorCases.response: The step is reported failed with 'posted, but its record was not written'; the next run lists the comments, finds the marker, records the kind and does not post again.
errorCases.userImpact: The author is told once; nothing is repeated on the issue.

errorCases.scenario: A second, different issue is offered for an artifact that is already bound
errorCases.detection: bindArtifact reads an existing binding whose reference names another issue
errorCases.response: Returns { ok: false, reason } naming both issues and changes nothing; ensureUnitIssueDetailed returns a before-create failure so the caller sees that the unit has two candidate issues.
errorCases.userImpact: A person must close one of the two issues; the unit never ends up bound to two.

errorCases.scenario: The link under the parent issue fails (Story under its Epic)
errorCases.detection: port.issueOps.linkSubIssue returns a failed result after the child was created or adopted
errorCases.response: setPendingLink stores { parent, childId } (or child when the id lookup failed); the next ensureUnitIssueDetailed retries it and clears it with setPendingLink(undefined) on success; the failure is logged and shown in the unit's result.
errorCases.userImpact: The unit is usable at once; its issue appears under the parent after the next retry.

errorCases.scenario: A file to attach has uncommitted changes or is not tracked by git
errorCases.detection: attachDocuments runs git status --porcelain for the path and finds output, or git log -1 --format=%H for the path prints nothing
errorCases.response: The target is reported in failed[] with 'commit the file first'; nothing is posted and nothing recorded. The calling approval path runs attachDocuments only after its commit step ran; when it did not (commitArtifacts is false, or the approval came through the daemon's workflow.approve, which commits nothing), the approval result says 'attachments skipped: the artifacts are not committed' and tracker.attach is run once they are.
errorCases.userImpact: The author commits and attaches again; the link always names a commit that holds the content shown.

errorCases.scenario: The unit has no binding when attachDocuments or recordPosted is called
errorCases.detection: readBinding returns undefined for the unit's artifact
errorCases.response: attachDocuments reports every target failed with 'the unit is not bound to an issue yet'; recordPosted returns false. Nothing is written.
errorCases.userImpact: A repository with no tracker has no binding and no attach is attempted.

errorCases.detection: TrackerPort.kind is not 'github' when listComments or attach is called
errorCases.response: The adapter for another kind answers a rejected 'unsupported' failure; attach is reported failed and nothing is posted.
errorCases.userImpact: Only GitHub is supported, as the owner ruled; no partial behaviour on other trackers.

errorCases.scenario: Two daemons create the same unit's issue at once
errorCases.detection: after its create, ensureUnitIssueDetailed lists the unit label with findIssues and finds more than one issue
errorCases.response: The lowest-numbered issue is bound once; this call's own issue, when it is not the lowest, is commented on and closed as a duplicate; when the listing fails the created issue is bound and kept and the duplicate check is reported as not run.
errorCases.userImpact: The unit ends bound to exactly one issue; the duplicate is closed with a pointer to the kept one.

errorCases.scenario: The head holding the binding cannot be read (malformed meta.envelope.binding, unreadable file)
errorCases.detection: decodeArtifactHead raises ArtifactShapeError, so ArtifactStore.read and update of that artifact fail as well as readBinding
errorCases.response: ensureUnitIssueDetailed calls readBinding on the unit's artifact before its local resolve; an ArtifactShapeError or an unreadable file there makes it return a before-create failure naming the head, before anything is looked up or created. resolveUnitIssueLocal (the gate's and the draft hook's read) catches the same error and reports no local issue, so those callers fall to ensure and get the same failure; isUnitSettled is false, so the draft hook reports not-ready with that reason.
errorCases.userImpact: The artifact is unreadable through the store until a person repairs the binding (or removes it, after which the next ensure rebinds through the unit label); no second issue is created.

errorCases.scenario: An approval path that does not commit calls for attachment (commitArtifacts false, or the daemon workflow.approve behind insrc_workflow_approve)
errorCases.detection: the TUI approve() reads cfg.commitArtifacts === false or commitApprovedArtifacts returns undefined; the daemon path has no commit step by design
errorCases.response: No attachDocuments call is made from that path; its result carries 'attachments skipped: the artifacts are not committed'. For a BUILD approval through the daemon, the followOn calls attachDocuments for the build, review and test records and reports each one the git check finds dirty.
errorCases.userImpact: The links are added by tracker.attach once the person or the build flow has committed the files; nothing is posted for a file that is not committed.

edgeCases.input: attachDocuments is called twice for an unchanged file
edgeCases.expected: The second call finds the Attachment for (target, revision) and reports it skipped; no tracker call is made.

edgeCases.input: An artifact is revised and committed, then attached again
edgeCases.expected: The commit sha changes, the link is new, a new comment is posted and a second Attachment is recorded; the first comment and Attachment stay.

edgeCases.input: A revision is made but not yet committed
edgeCases.expected: The file is dirty, so the target is refused; the earlier attachment remains valid.

edgeCases.input: The attach comment was posted but the Attachment was not recorded
edgeCases.expected: The next attachDocuments finds a comment holding the same link in listComments, records the Attachment with that comment's id as externalId, and reports it reconciled.

edgeCases.input: A comment on the issue quotes the marker text of a framework post
edgeCases.expected: It is treated as the post (the marker is the key); the framework posts its markers at the start of the body and only comments authored through the tracker whose text starts with the marker count.

edgeCases.input: A person created the issue first and the framework adopts it
edgeCases.expected: The Epic or Story artifact is bound to that issue through the label or title lookup; createdAtRevision is the head's revision at that moment.

edgeCases.input: A repository has no tracker configuration
edgeCases.expected: No lookup, create, bind, post or attach is attempted and the artifacts carry no binding.

edgeCases.input: A Task unit asks for its issue
edgeCases.expected: The Task's record is read and written on the Plan's meta.tracker.units as before, with pendingLink retry; s7 moves it to the Task artifact's binding.

edgeCases.input: A head written before s6 has meta.tracker.units but no binding
edgeCases.expected: readBinding returns undefined; resolveUnitIssueLocal reads the older ref, binds the unit from it, and the old approve-time marks are not read (a design, review or plan comment may be posted once more unless it carries the new marker); s9 converts what remains.

edgeCases.input: Two comment steps of one unit are both unrecorded
edgeCases.expected: listComments is read once and shared across both steps.

edgeCases.input: Two daemons create a unit's issue at the same moment
edgeCases.expected: Both lists show both issues; both calls bind the lowest-numbered one; the other call's issue is closed as a duplicate; the unit has one binding.

edgeCases.input: A pre-s6 Epic or Story whose only record is epicRef, storyRef or meta.tracker.units
edgeCases.expected: resolveUnitIssueLocal finds the issue through the older ref and binds the unit from it once; the draft hook, the gate and the handoff check then resolve it from the binding; no lookup and no second issue are needed.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A Task's issue record, its pending link and its retry keep working unchanged on the Plan until s7: the Epic and Story change must not alter a Task unit's behaviour.
A failed lookup is a failure, never 'not found': ensureUnitIssueDetailed creates nothing when a lookup, the title guard or the parent lookup failed.
The unit's issue is found again by its label or title after a crash, so a lost local record never produces a second issue.
Tracker access stays through the gh CLI only: listComments and attach add no direct REST call and no new credential.
The team gate decides on the tracker's live identity and the unit's issue; reading the binding changes neither, and the gate's synchronous path stays synchronous.

migration.stateBefore: Unit-issue bookkeeping is a loose record under meta.tracker.units on the Define (Epic), the LLD (Story) or the Plan (Task): issue ref, createdAtRevision, a pendingLink for a failed parent link, and extrasDone marks for the approve-time posts (src/workflow/tracker/refs.ts:26-47, src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts:176-197 and :518-576). A post is marked after it succeeds, so a crash between the post and its mark repeats the post. The tracker port has no listComments and no attach; the envelope's binding and attachments fields exist (src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts:155-181) and are read and validated but never written.
migration.stateAfter: An Epic's Define and a Story's LLD carry a typed binding (meta.envelope.binding) written by one set of functions, and any artifact can carry attachments; the approve-time comments carry a marker and are reconciled through listComments before a retry, so no post repeats. The port has listComments and attach for GitHub. A content write by the store carries the on-disk binding and attachments. A Task unit keeps its legacy record on the Plan until s7. Existing meta.tracker.epicRef, storyRef, storyRefs, taskRefs and pushedAt are still written for the renderers and the chain report; s9 converts them.

migrationSteps.action: Add the TrackerComment type, listComments and attach to the tracker port, the GitHub adapter and the in-memory fakes; additive, no caller yet.

Add the binding module (readBinding, bindArtifact, recordPosted, setPendingLink) as meta-only patches of meta.envelope, and the carryBinding rule in the content branch of the storage write so a store write keeps the on-disk binding and attachments; additive, no caller yet.
Add the permalink and attachDocuments, with the dirty-file and tracked-file checks and the reconcile-by-link step; no caller yet.

Switch ensureUnitIssueDetailed, resolveUnitIssueLocal, isUnitSettled and the pending-link retry for an Epic or Story unit from meta.tracker.units to the binding; a Task unit keeps its record. A head with only the old record has no binding, so the next ensure finds its issue by the unit label or title and binds it. A created issue is bound after the duplicate check (tieBreak binds the lowest-numbered issue once). resolveUnitIssueLocal keeps the epicRef, storyRef and storyRefs fallback only as a one-way rebind source for a unit with no binding; draft-issues.ts and team/handoff.ts follow it through resolveUnitIssueLocal.

Switch runUnitExtras to the binding's posted list for an Epic or Story, add the comment markers to the design, review and plan comment bodies in tracker-auto, and reconcile an unrecorded comment step through one listComments read before posting; remove extrasDone from UnitIssue.

Add the tracker.attach daemon method. Call attachDocuments from the TUI approve() after its commit step for the HLD, LLD and plan documents (their diagram companions are attached by tracker.attach once committed), committing the attachment records in a second commit; skip it with a stated reason when commitArtifacts is false. Call it from the daemon's BUILD approval followOn for the build, review and test records, only for files git reports clean. The follow-on outcome union in src/workflow/gates.ts:827-832 gains a 'tracker-attach' kind carrying the AttachOutcome, wired at both follow-on sites in src/daemon/index.ts (workflow.approve at :652 and workflow.reviewDecision at :744).

Update the tests that seed or assert Epic or Story records under meta.tracker.units or extrasDone: src/workflow/tracker/__tests__/unit-issue.test.ts, src/workflow/tracker/__tests__/unit-extras.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/tracker-auto.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/approve-fallback-issues.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/draft-issues.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/redraft-preserves-tracker.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/artifact-writer.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/gate-approve.test.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/pending.test.ts, src/daemon/__tests__/draft-issues-synthesize.test.ts, src/cli/__tests__/run-readiness-notice.test.ts, src/cli/__tests__/services.test.ts and src/cli/__tests__/team-claim-release.test.ts (a grep for units and extrasDone in the tests finds these; each is checked), and record the s9 conversion inputs in docs/plans/core-data-model.md.

migration.backwardCompat: No compatibility code is written (owner ruling). The IPC surface gains the tracker.attach method and the 'tracker-attach' follow-on outcome kind (additive); no existing method or result shape changes. Heads written before s6 carry meta.tracker.units with extrasDone but no binding: the next ensure rebinds the Epic or Story through the label or title lookup, and the old approve-time marks are not read, so an old unit's design, review or plan comment may be posted once more unless its comment already carries the new marker; s9 converts the old records into bindings and marks before that matters. meta.tracker.epicRef, storyRef, storyRefs, taskRefs and pushedAt keep being written for the markdown renderers and the chain report until s9. The older epicRef, storyRef and storyRefs stay readable as a one-way rebind source for an Epic or Story unit with no binding until s9.

alternativesConsidered.name: Binding on the envelope through a BindingService, marker-reconciled posts
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A small service over ArtifactStore reads and updates the envelope's typed binding and attachments; every post carries a stable marker and is reconciled through listComments before a retry.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add src/workflow/tracker/binding-service.ts: BindingService { bind(artifactId, issueRef, by), read(artifactId), recordPosted(artifactId, kind, externalId?), setPendingLink(artifactId, link | undefined), attach(artifactId, target, port, links) } built on ArtifactStore.update (the binding and attachments are envelope fields, so they move no revision and add one change-log entry without a content hash change). Extend TrackerPort with listComments(issue, since?) and attach(issue, artifact, link), both implemented for the GitHub adapter only through the gh CLI (attach on GitHub is a comment that carries the permalink and a marker '<!-- insrc:attach:<artifactId>:r<revision> -->'; no attachment API exists). Post markers '<!-- insrc:post:<artifactId>:<kind> -->' are put in the comment bodies the approve-time extras already write; before running a post whose kind is not in binding.posted, the runner calls listComments and, if a comment with the marker exists, records the post (externalId = the comment id) and does not post again; otherwise it posts, then records. unit-issue.ts resolveUnitIssueLocal/recordUnit/retryPendingLink/runUnitExtras switch from meta.tracker.units to the binding for Epic and Story artifacts; a Task's record (no artifact until s7) stays under the Plan's meta.tracker.units behind the same function signatures, and s7 moves it. The permalink is blob/<commit sha>/<path> where the sha is the last commit that touched the file (git log -1 --format=%H -- <path>), built privately in this Story.
pros: Meets all three acceptance criteria and both functional requirements as the HLD states them
The binding is typed, validated by the store, and merges like any envelope field
Reconciling before a retry closes the post-then-crash repeat that the current mark-after-post design documents as a residual
Reuses the store, the existing marker habit and the gh path; adds no storage format
cons: Two homes for unit records until s7 (Epic and Story on the binding, Task rows on the Plan)
A marker check costs one listComments call per unmarked post on retry
unit-issue.ts, tracker-auto.ts and their tests change

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep meta.tracker.units, add attachments and the two port methods
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Leave the loose UnitIssue records alone; add an attachments list beside them and listComments/attach on the port.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do not touch the binding field on the envelope. Add listComments and attach to TrackerPort and the GitHub adapter, add an attachments array to meta.tracker (an Attachment-shaped list), and have the attach caller record each link there. Posts and pending links stay in extrasDone and pendingLink as today.
pros: Smallest change; almost no existing code or test moves
cons: Leaves the loose tracker fields the Story exists to replace; the binding on the envelope stays unused
Does not close the post-then-crash repeat (mark still follows the post, no reconciliation)
The s7 Task artifact and the s8 comment sync would build on an untyped record
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest but fails the typed-record requirement and leaves the repeat-post gap (rank 3 in s3: partial on ac17 and ac19, violates sc2).

alternativesConsidered.name: Binding plus a durable posting receipt line file
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, but once-only posting is kept in a new append-only sidecar of receipts keyed by what was posted, not by a marker comment check.
alternativesConsidered.approach: BindingService as in a1, plus a new receipts sidecar (append-only lines keyed by artifact id and post kind) written before the post is sent and completed after, with a reconcile step that reads the receipts. Reuses the s4 SidecarStore for storage and merge rules.
pros: A receipt exists before the remote call, so a crash is always detectable locally
No dependence on reading the remote comments back
cons: A third sidecar file kind and merge rule beyond the HLD (a new sc5 file), so an HLD amendment owned by s4's boundary
A receipt cannot tell whether the remote post happened when the crash was in between; reconciliation still needs listComments
More storage for the same guarantee
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Works but needs a third sidecar kind owned by s4's boundary and does not remove the need to read comments back (rank 2 in s3: partial on ac19).

openQuestions: The binding and attachments are written by sync meta-only patches, not through ArtifactStore.update, because the team gate and the draft-issue hook that record a unit's issue are synchronous and the store is async; making them async would rewrite every teamGate caller. To keep a store write from undoing a patch, prepareArtifactWrite carries meta.envelope.binding and meta.envelope.attachments from the head on disk into every content write of an existing artifact (carryBinding, as carryTracker does for meta.tracker). That touches the store's write path owned by s2 and s4. Resolve: accept it as an s6-owned change to src/workflow/storage.ts (recommended), or move the two sync recording points to the async store and make the gate async (a large change outside s6).

Binding and attachment bookkeeping appends no change log entry, although the HLD's observability line says every state change does; the record is in the binding itself (posted[].at, attachments[].at) and the log output. Resolve: accept this as tracker bookkeeping rather than artifact state (recommended), or add an Operation for it and have a sync path append through History (needs an HLD amendment to sc3).

A Task unit keeps its issue record on the Plan's meta.tracker.units until s7 creates Task artifacts, so unit-issue.ts has two homes for a record (binding for Epic and Story, the Plan for Task). Resolve: accept for now and have s7 move Task records onto the Task artifact's binding (recommended), or have s6 create the Task artifacts (that is s7's scope).

Until s9 creates Epic and Story artifacts, an Epic's binding sits on the Define and a Story's on the LLD (the artifacts that hold the unit's record today). Resolve: accept and record in docs/plans/core-data-model.md that s9 moves each binding onto the Epic and Story artifact it creates (recommended).

A permalink names the last commit that touched the file but the commit may not be pushed, so the link is dead on GitHub until it is. Resolve: accept; the sha link becomes valid when the commit is pushed (recommended), or refuse to attach until the commit is on a remote branch.

No step commits the build, review and test records: the TUI approve() commits only the Define for a BUILD, and the daemon workflow.approve commits nothing. s6 adds no commit. The BUILD approval's followOn calls attachDocuments for those records and the new tracker.attach method attaches them on demand, in each case only for files git reports clean (the build flow's controller commits the records before approval, as it does for the s4 and s5 BUILD and TESTS records). Resolve: accept (recommended), or add a commit of the Story's records to the BUILD completion path (a change to the build gate outside s6).
